what: 船坞 at 四宜书屋 / 安澜园: four docks of 13 bays
where: north shore of 福海, south side of 安澜园, screened by ground to the south
by: Qing texts quoted in the article
locator: section 圆明园四宜书屋藏舟坞
summary_en: Quoted: "查圆明园现有船坞四座，每座十三间" and "……西峰秀色往东，东西船坞各二所，北岸为四宜书屋，五楹即安澜园……". Size quoted: "檐柱各高一丈一尺五寸，径一尺；金柱各高一丈五尺三寸，径一尺一寸" (eaves columns 11.5 chi = 3.68 m, inner columns 15.3 chi = 4.90 m at 0.32 m). The Qianlong 40 workshop record puts the barge 翔凤艇 at this dock.
status: verified (as quoted in the article; primary texts not seen)

what: 船坞 at 方壶胜境 and the boats' way in
where: south-east of 方壶胜境, mouth facing north; boats came from the west (安澜园), called at 迎薰亭, entered the dock or passed the plank bridge on the south into 福海
by: Qing text quoted in the article
summary_en: Quoted: "……哕莺殿东为蕊珠宫，宫南船塢後有龍王廟". The route from 安澜园 by 迎薰亭 and the south plank bridge into 福海 is the article's reading, not a quote.

what: 藻园 船坞: a 13-bay two-storey building, the centre of the group; change from road to boat
where: 藻园, south-west corner of 圆明园: water route from 畅春园, imperial road to 清漪园 / 万寿山
by: Qing records quoted in the article
summary_en: Quoted (Qianlong 21 dress record): "……乘四人亮轿出船坞门，至万寿山游行毕，回来，进藻园门内乘船……"; Qianlong 30: "……传旨藻园十三间楼下扇面墙……". The dock mouth faced away from the court and 粹藻楼 screened it (article).

what: 藏舟坞 of 万方安和, reached over a plank bridge
where: west of the 卍 hall, behind the west hill; boats passed a wooden plank bridge 木板桥 / 盖板桥 to the lake
by: Qing record quoted in the article
summary_en: Quoted: "……将藏舟坞匾挂在万方安和船坞。钦此。"

what: 南船坞 of 曲院风荷: 13 bays, door to the east, boats into 福海
where: south of the 曲院风荷 lotus pond, across the water from the main court
by: article reading the Forty Scenes leaf
summary_en: Thirteen bays, door to the east, boats reach 福海 from here (article).

what: 鉴园 船坞: the only dock in 长春园, 13 bays
where: behind 鉴园, south-east 长春园, next to 如园
by: Qing record quoted in the article
summary_en: Quoted: "……臣等谨案鉴园之后有船坞" (日下旧闻考) and "……拆砌后檐墙船坞一座十三间，拆瓦头停……".

what: count of historical bridges and what survives
where: the three gardens inside today's park
by: 清华同衡 建筑与城市遗产研究所 (肖金亮, 殷丽娜)
source_id: NEW: 清华同衡 建筑与城市遗产研究所, 圆明园考古遗址公园 历史桥梁形制研究, 2017-09; https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202007/t20200729_4416663.html
locator: PDF p.237 (printed 235), table 桥梁数量分类统计表
summary_en: 190 historical bridges in the table (191 in the text): 131 YM, 41 QC, 18 CC; 123 gone; 6 in place in original form, 84 in place rebuilt otherwise, 45 new off the historical site; 2 ruined bridges survive (1 QC, 1 CC). Types: stone pier with timber beams, timber beam bridges, stone arch and stone beam bridges (p.13).

what: plans used by the bridge study to place every bridge

what: Tongzhi 13 (1874) order: 抄手游廊 and bridges at 清夏堂 and 寄情咸畅
where: 清夏堂 (万春园) and 寄情咸畅

what: 如园 drawings: 如园[地盘全样] 样385-0015 and 延清堂 地盘样 / 地盘尺寸样

what: 长春园全图准底

by: Yangshi Lei

status: verified (title and date as cited); content unknown

what: 长春园绮春园圆明园三园地盘河道全图 (Palace Museum)
where: three gardens
by: Yangshi Lei, Palace Museum

what: 泽兰堂 plan: removal of 理性居 and its galleries 游廊
where: 泽兰堂, 长春园
by: Yangshi Lei, NLC 样076-3
summary_en: Title: "道光十五年七月十五日奏准拆去理性居并游廊改安巡杖栏杆": galleries here were removed in 1835 and replaced by railings; so not to be modelled for 1860.

what: 九洲清晏 court sizes in 丈尺
where: 九洲清晏 courts
by: Yangshi Lei, NLC 006-3 and 062-24
summary_en: Court sizes of every court of the scene, for the Tongzhi repair; not opened. B for 1860 (Q36).

what: Musée Guimet plan 圆明园地盘全图
where: whole Yuanming Yuan
by: Qing plan, Musée Guimet; studied by 王其亨, 张凤梧
summary_en: Its last state shows the 1858 change of 慎德堂's west gallery, so it is close to the eve of 1860; whether it draws paths and their widths is not known here.

what: 1933 survey map 实测圆明园长春园万春园遗址形势图
where: three gardens, 1:2,000, colour, 150 x 106 cm
by: 北平市政府工务局
summary_en: Press: the first modern survey; draws hills, waters and the places of bridges and culverts closest to the original; after setting boundary stones the surveyors probed the ruins and drew the buildings on their sites. Whether it draws paths or roads of the Qing garden: not stated; no scan seen. The 长春园 gate dig corrected details of it (E0007).

what: 中国营造学社 black-and-white films of Qing plans (PPxxx series)
where: three gardens and single scenes
by: 中国营造学社 (films), now cited by 清华同衡

where: whole garden
year: state about Daoguang to Xianfeng; drawn or traced 1920s
by: unknown artist; Malone
summary_en: Draws halls by bays, court walls, gates, galleries as one-bay rows, steps as bracket marks, bridges as strips; paths in open courts are mostly not drawn (repo reading, Round 9 brief). B in this project.

what: step and paving terms found in the 如园 report
where: 延清堂
summary_en: 垂带踏跺 steps with sloping side slabs (front); 抄手踏跺 steps on both sides of a terrace; 云步踏跺 cloud steps of rough Taihu rock; 石片散水 apron of thin stone slabs; 金砖墁地 polished floor tiles; 阶条石 kerb slabs (0.576 m wide on the south terrace).

status: verified (repo row, as quoted by S220)

what: 平台码头 a terrace landing; 游廊 galleries of 涵远斋 and 明善堂

what: 船坞 before Qichun joined: 春和园 (Fuheng's garden) had a dock by 清吟书屋 and a boat ride to 锦香亭
where: later 绮春园, 明善堂 area
by: 毕沅, 春和园纪游, quoted in S220

what: 线法山 Xianfa Shan: regularly intersecting circular paths to the top pavilion; the emperor rode up
where: the round hill east of the 大水法 group
by: Malone
summary_en: Quoted: "Regularly intersecting circular paths led up to the pavilion on the top of this circular hill ... The old caretaker Lu said the Emperor ascended the hill on horseback." Engraving 18 is the period source.

what: Xiyang Lou: formal, symmetrically paved paths; the paved north court of 谐奇趣
where: gardens nearest the European buildings; north front of 谐奇趣
by: Malone
summary_en: Quoted: "The parts of the gardens nearest to the buildings were laid out in a very formal manner, with conventionally trimmed trees, and symmetrically paved paths" and "The north front of the Hsieh Ch'i Ch'ü faced on a fantastically paved courtyard". The engraving itself is A.

summary_en: Quoted: "three marble terraces extend into the lake with stairs leading to the water's edge to meet the imperial barge" and "A bridge in the center and two piers at the side connected this lower terrace with three smaller terraces which extended into the lake ... steps led down to the water's edge to welcome the imperial barge"; "elevated walks connecting their second stories". The leaf (S08) is the A source.

what: boathouses north of 福海

by: Malone
summary_en: Quoted: "It was very close to the boathouses north of the Happy Sea." Agrees with the four 13-bay docks of the archives (S42 row).
